messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: P0 pager from runtime-alerts: serving-runtime-prod error rate spike -> 502s and CrashLoopBackOffs on gpu-serving pools. Trigger: GPU OOM + autoscaler flapping. Root ts: 1781234567
Maya (oncall): I'm on it. I'm seeing repeated CrashLoopBackOffs for model-server pods in gpu-pool-eu.
Tom: Confirming, autoscaler logs show scale events every ~30s, nodes coming up then down, kubelet evicting pods -> crashloops. This looks like capacity thrash.
Lee (runtime): Logs from a pod: ```[2026-03-15T10:22:11Z] runtime ERROR: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY trying to alloc 1.2GB (device 0)
stack: at cuda.cu:open_tensor
Model init failure -> container exits with code 137
```
Sofia (sre): Crash reason code 137 usually OOM killed by kernel oom. But the CUDA OOM suggests GPU memory fragmentation from batching. Autoscaler thrash likely amplifying startup pressure.
Maya (oncall): Quick assessment: impact visible on /v1/generate endpoints for some customers -> increased latency and 50-70% error rates for requests routed to that pool. CS notified.
Jordan (CS): We have 3 mid-market customers seeing errors, two using dedicated capacity in eu-west region. They're being paged. ETA to share with customers?
Maya (oncall): Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Pause autoscaler scaling up/down for gpu-pool-eu (set replicas fixed) 2) Prevent new pods from hitting unstable nodes 3) Rollback to older image without aggressive batching 4) Enable CPU fallback routes
Tom: Doing 1) now: ```kubectl patch hpa gpu-pool-eu-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3,"maxReplicas":3}}'``` -> patch applied. Not removing nodes, just stabilizing replica count.
Ravi (eng-platform): I'll cordon the flaky nodes and drain pods carefully to avoid thundering restarts. Running: ```kubectl cordon node-eu-7 && kubectl drain node-eu-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```
Lee (runtime): For rollback: new image tag 2.14 had a batching change. Roll back to 2.13 which uses safer dynamic batching defaults. Creating a rollout: ```kubectl set image deployment/model-server model-server=rgcr/redwood/model-server:2.13```
Maya (oncall): Applying 2) prevent new pods on unstable nodes: taint nodes with runtime-unstable=true:NoSchedule for node-eu-7,8.
Sofia (sre): Also dropping aggressive pod startup parallelism on the deployment: set maxSurge=0, maxUnavailable=1 to slow rollout.
Nina (devex-bot): Noted. Routing rules updated: fallback-route cpu-pool-eu enabled for model.family:small and model.family:medium.
Jordan (CS): Sending customer update: "We're seeing increased errors in the EU serving pool due to GPU OOMs triggered by rapid autoscaling. We're stabilizing capacity and rolling back a recent batching change. ETA 15-30m for most traffic to recover"
Maya (oncall): Monitoring: error rate decreasing from 65% -> 30% after patching HPA and rollback started. Still seeing occasional OOMs on startup.
Tom: Observed that when nodes scale up they sometimes come with older nvidia-drivers from AMI bake -> causes fallback/memory mismatch. Ravi, can we enforce node image consistency?
Ravi (eng-platform): Yes, we'll pin node group to the golden AMI and drain non-compliant nodes. Creating a ticket for infra automation.
Lee (runtime): Action item: add a safe-start flag to model server to preallocate smaller KV cache on startup and refuse large batch sizes until warm. Will prototype.
Sofia (sre): Post-incident notes: probable causes: 1) new batching defaults in 2.14 increased initial GPU allocation leading to OOM on cold-start; 2) autoscaler aggressive scaling policy (cooldown 30s) produced scale flapping under request bursts causing many concurrent startups; 3) node image inconsistency occasionally changed CUDA driver behavior.
Maya (oncall): Current status: degraded but recovering. Next steps: follow-up bug for batching defaults, autoscaler cooldown increase to 5m, AMI pinning, and platform change to prefer rolling restarts that stagger pod startups.
Jordan (CS): Customers updated. Will follow up if any major regressions.
IncidentBot: Incident marked: mitigated -> monitoring (P0 -> P1). Close ETA: 2026-03-15T11:00:00Z."
